summary: Iteration 34: Verified fixes for TWO PRODUCTION BUGS - (1) Rate limiter now uses X-Forwarded-For via get_client_ip() with MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS=50, (2) CORS configured without allow_credentials for Firefox/Edge compatibility. All 19 backend tests passed. All UI tests passed including login, session persistence, and logout.

login_returns_access_token: ✓ Admin login returns access_token in response body
✓ Developer login returns access_token in response body
multiple_simultaneous_logins: ✓ 20 sequential logins all return 200 (rate limit of 50 allows this)
rate_limiter_configuration: ✓ get_client_ip reads X-Forwarded-For and X-Real-IP headers
✓ Login route uses get_client_ip for rate limiting
cors_configuration: ✓ CORS does NOT have Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
✓ Actual POST request has correct CORS headers

bug_1_rate_limiter.problem: Rate limiter was using request.client.host which returns Railway proxy IP, causing all users behind proxy to share same IP limit of 15
bug_1_rate_limiter.fix: Changed to get_client_ip() which reads X-Forwarded-For header to get real client IP, increased MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS to 50
verification: get_client_ip function exists at line ~48 in server.py
get_client_ip reads x-forwarded-for and x-real-ip headers
Login route calls get_client_ip(request) at line ~661

bug_2_cors_firefox_edge.problem: CORS had allow_credentials=True with allow_origins=['*'] which Firefox/Edge block per CORS spec
bug_2_cors_firefox_edge.fix: Removed allow_credentials from CORS middleware, removed withCredentials from frontend, use Bearer token from localStorage as primary auth
verification: CORS middleware at line ~3941 has allow_origins=['*'] without allow_credentials
AuthContext.js sets Bearer Authorization header from localStorage
CORS response does NOT contain 'access-control-allow-credentials: true'

critical_code_review_comments: Rate limiter now properly identifies individual users behind Railway proxy
CORS configuration is now compatible with all browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
Bearer token auth via localStorage is the primary auth mechanism
Cookie auth is secondary fallback with samesite=none
seed_data_creation: No seed data created - tests use existing admin and developer accounts
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 34 verified fixes for TWO PRODUCTION BUGS: (1) Rate limiter now uses get_client_ip() which reads X-Forwarded-For header, MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS=50 allows multiple users from same network. (2) CORS configured with allow_origins=['*'] WITHOUT allow_credentials, frontend uses Bearer token from localStorage (no withCredentials). Both admin and developer logins work. Session persists after page refresh via localStorage. All 19 backend tests and 6 UI tests passed.
